Shri Sohit Mishra - Government Advocate for the petitioners
 Shri Jitendra Sharma - learned Senior Advocate with Ms. Kra
 Advocate for the respondent.

Order 
Per: Justice Anand Pathak
1.
Heard on I.A. No.8269/2025, an application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act.
2. As per office note, the petition is barred by 387 days.
3. It is the submission of learned counsel for the petitioners that present review petition is preferred after delay of 387 days because of the reasons assigned into the applicaiton.

4. Learned counsel for the respondent opposed the prayer and submits that when the order dated 12th July, 2024 was passed in Writ Appeal No.1119/2022 and Writ Appeal No.1120/2022, then it was the duty of the review petitioners to file the review petition immediately thereafter.

Therefore,
delay cannot be condoned.

1 5.

Considering the submissions advanced and in the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case,
I.A. is allowed.
Delay in filing the petition is hereby condoned.
6. With the consent of the parties, heard on merits.

7. The instant review petition under Order 47 Rule 1 CPC is filed seeking review of the order dated 12th July, 2024 passed in Writ Appeal No.1119/2022 and Writ Appeal No.1120/2022 whereby writ appeal preferred by the respondent was allowed and in consequence thereof, Rs.2 Lacs have been directed to be paid by the review petitioners/ State as compensation to the sole respondent.
8.

It is the submission of learned Government Advocate for the review petitioners/ State that matter pertains to alleged encroachment in which respondent claiming himself to the owner and possessor of the temple and nearby land bearing Survey No.2613 at Datia being a disciple of Mahant of that temple.

Respondent was served upon a notice dated 09/07/2010 issued by SDO/ Additional Tehsildar PWD, Datia alleging that respondent encroached upon the government land bearing survey no.2255 and explanation was sought.

But without concluding the proceedings under Section 248 of the M.P. Land Revenue Code, 1959, petitioners/State demolished 14 shops which resulted into loss of Rs.40 lacs to the respondent as well as occupants of the shops.

Against the same,
respondent file Writ Petition No.7667/2010 and Writ Petition No.4120/2010, in which interim protection was given to the respondent.

However, the said writ petitions were dismissed vide order d a t e d 2 3 / 0 8 / 2 0 2 2 o n t h e g r o u n d t h a t p e t i t i o n e r N E U T R A L C I T A T I O N N O .
2025:MPHC-GWL:28246 3 RP-2020-2025 (respondent herein) has not challenged the final order dated 16/07/2010 and deity is the owner of survey no.2613 and petitioner has no locus standi to file the writ petition.
However, liberty was granted to the deity to challenge the final order dated 16/07/2010 through its next friend.

9. Against the said order, respondent filed Writ Appeal No.1120/2022, but vide non-speaking order dated 22/09/2022, the same was dismissed, thus, persuaded the respondent to approach the Hon'ble Apex Court by way of filing SLP vide SLP(c) No.5374/2023 and vide order dated 15/04/2024,
SLP was allowed and the Writ Appellate was directed to decide the matter on merits.
10. The learned Writ Appellate Court discussed all relevant laws and judgments pronounced in this regard and came to the conclusion that shops of the respondent have been demolished illegally.
During promulgation of the stay order, review petitioners/ State proceeded against the present respondent and demolished the shops.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.2 lacs was imposed upon the petitioners/ State to be given to the present respondent.
This prompted the petitioners/ State to file the instant review petition which is otherwise barred by time.
11. Learned counsel for the respondent opposed the prayer and submits that the review petition not only suffers from delay and latches but also on merits.
During proceedings pending before Writ Court, stay was granted to the respondent from dispossession, but still review petitioners/ State proceeded and demolished the shops of the respondent.
All these facts were discussed in the Writ A p p e l l a t e o r d e r i n d e t a i l , t h e r e f o r e , n o c a s e f o r N E U T R A L C I T A T I O N N O .

Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the documents appended thereto.
13. Scope of review is well-defined.
In the case of Kamlesh Verma Vs. Mayawati and Others, (2013) 8 SCC 320, principles relating to review jurisdiction have been laid down.

entities.text: Kamlesh Verma Vs. Mayawati and Others, (2013) 8 SCC 320
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The words "any other sufficient reason" have been interpreted in Chhajju Ram Vs. Neki, (1921-22)
49 IA 144 and approved by this Court in the case of Moran Mar Basselios Catholicos Vs. Most Rev.
Mar Poulose Athanasius, AIR 1954 SC 526 to mean "a reason sufficient on grounds at least analogous to those specified in the rule".
When the review will not be maintainable:
"(i) A repetition of old and overruled argument is not enough to reopen concluded adjudications.

entities.text:
Moran Mar Basselios Catholicos Vs. Most Rev.
Mar Poulose Athanasius, AIR 1954 SC 526
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (ii) Minor mistakes of inconsequential import.
(iii) Review proceedings cannot be equated with the original hearing NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:28246 5 RP-2020-2025 of the case.
(iv) Review is not maintainable unless the material error, manifest on the face of order, undermines its soundness or results in miscarriage of justice.
(v) A review is by no means an appeal in disguise whereby an erroneous decision is reheard and corrected but lies only for patent error.
(vi) The mere possibility of two views on the subject cannot be a ground for review.
(vii) The error apparent on the face of the record should not be an error which has to be fished out and searched.

sentences.text: 3 (viii) The appreciation of evidence on record is fully within the domain of the appellate Court, it cannot be permitted to be advanced in the review petition.
(ix) Reviews is not maintainable when the same relief sought at the time of arguing the main matter had been negatived.

15. It is also held by the Apex Court in the case of State of West Bengal & Ors. Vs. Kamal Sengupta &
Anr., (2008) 8 SCC 612 that mistake or error apparent on the face of the record means that mistake or error which is prima facie visible and does not require any detail examination.

sentences.text: Erroneous view of law is not a ground for review and review cannot partake the category of the appeal."
16. If the scope of review is tested on the anvil of factual details then it appears that review petition is misconceived.

The Writ Appellate Court rightly held that review petitioners/ State proceeded arbitrarily and in NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:28246 6 RP-2020-2025 flagrant violation of the stay order granted by the Writ Court, therefore, imposition of compensation is not excessive or arbitrary.
Shops of the respondent were demolished on the pretext of road widening and even review petitioners/State did not care to consider the case for compensation under the Land Acquisition Act.

17. Looking to the high handedness of the review petitioners/State, findings arrived at by the Appellate Court regarding imposition of compensation is just and proper and the same needs no interreference.

No documents has been placed by the review petitioners/ State to show that they proceeded in the matter in accordance with law and in absence of any such pleadings and documents, only inference can be drawn is that the Writ Appellate Court rightly considered the case and imposed the compensation of Rs.2 lacs upon petitioners/State.
18. In the cumulative analysis of the case, no case for interference is made out.
29. Review petition stands dismissed.
